{{< include _extensions/r-wasm/live/_knitr.qmd >}}

This page is a demonstration, not a chapter.  It runs **real R in your browser** — no
installation, no server.  The first cell takes a few seconds to start while R loads; after
that it is quick.

Everything below is editable.  Change a number, press *Run Code*, and see what happens.

## 1. A cell you can edit

The simplest case: a few yields, and a mean.  Try changing one of the numbers, or adding
another, and re-running.

```{webr}
yields <- c(48, 52, 47, 55, 50)
mean(yields)
```

## 2. Building a chart one layer at a time

This is the sort of thing that is hard to teach on a printed page.  Run it, then add
`+ geom_smooth(method = "lm")` on a new line and run it again.

```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: plot1
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
d <- read.csv("practice/data/sask_variety_yields.csv")
d <- d[!is.na(d$Yield) & !is.na(d$Acres) & d$Year == 2025, ]
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: plot1
ggplot(d[d$Crop == "Barley", ], aes(x = Acres, y = Yield)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#4a7c59", alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "Acres seeded", y = "Yield (bu/ac)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 3. An exercise with a hint

Compute the mean barley yield for 2025.  The data frame `d` is already loaded and filtered
to 2025.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_mean
barley <- d[d$Crop == "Barley", ]
______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_mean" }
You want `mean()` of the `Yield` column.  Remember `$` selects a column.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_mean" }
```r
mean(barley$Yield)
```
:::

## 4. Seeing a mistake happen

The silent-join failure from @sec-ai-silent-failure, live.  Run this and look at how many
rows come back with a price.

```{webr}
#| exercise: join1
prices <- data.frame(
  Crop = c("Canola", "Spring wheat", "Barley", "Oats"),
  Price = c(14.00, 8.00, 5.50, 4.50)
)

j <- merge(d, prices, by = "Crop", all.x = TRUE)
sum(!is.na(j$Price))   # how many rows found a price?
nrow(j)                # out of how many?
```

Now fix it: change `"Canola"` to `"Canola/Rapeseed"` in the price table and run it again.

## What this costs

The R runtime downloads once per visitor (a few MB, cached afterwards), and each package
adds to that.  ggplot2 and dplyr are the two that matter for this course.  Pages without
`{webr}` cells are unaffected.
